A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLAPP++ research, and their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. V1's appendices A–D correspond to v2's B–E; v2 adds an algorithm appendix and further theoretical and experimental material.

before.justification: V1 reports original gradient-alignment simulations, image-classification experiments in Table 2, and additional predictive-coding and ablation results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet classification results and resource-efficiency comparisons.

M1.justification: CLAPP++, CLAPP++DFB and the summed-loss CLAPP++both variant already appear in v1. V2 formalizes the existing spatial pooling and feedback construction and documents equivalent execution procedures; it does not establish a changed learning rule.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet representation learning and downstream classification to the retained CIFAR-10, STL-10 and Tiny ImageNet evaluations. This substantially extends the empirical coverage to a harder, higher-resolution benchmark; the MNIST simulations remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SoftHebb (Journé et al., 2023) as a reported comparator, with CIFAR-10, STL-10 and ImageNet accuracies of 80.31, 76.23 and 27.3. The existing comparison methods are retained; the citation and table do not establish that SoftHebb was rerun.

E3.justification: The new ImageNet protocol uses eight convolutional layers with doubled VGG11 widths, 224-pixel inputs, batch size 256, and 100 epochs with LARS. Table 3 introduces an activation-memory and iteration-time evaluation at batch size 256. For the original three benchmarks, the stated training batch size changes from 32 to 128; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects documentation or reflects rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: V1 defers resource-efficiency analysis to future work; v2 adds a substantive comparison of activation-memory requirements and iteration times for BP and ideal local implementations on STL-10 and ImageNet. It also tests the spatial-dependence and feedback ablations on ImageNet. The existing rank constraints, gradient-alignment analyses and training-stage plots are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 95% confidence intervals from four random-seed simulations for Table 2 entries carrying uncertainty, and retain the existing figure uncertainty reporting. V2 introduces no new seed-count or statistical-testing procedure. Its added ImageNet scores have no reported confidence intervals.

E6.justification: New ImageNet accuracies are 42.55 for CLAPP++, 44.16 for CLAPP++DFB and 42.49 for CLAPP++both, versus 48.52 for BP-CLAPP++ and 55.19 for BP-InfoNCE. Thus DFB leads the local variants there, but a BP gap remains. Existing scores are retained, while Table 3 adds resource results. The new CIFAR-10 predictive-coding entry of 46.52 in Table 2 is unreconciled with 45.62 in the retained appendix comparison.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition 3.5 and its Appendix B.3 proof, constructing a spatially dependent feedback operator that can reproduce BP gradients in linear convolutional networks with unit pooling patches. It also explains why global pooling cannot generally do so. V1 supplied intuition and simulations for this case, rather than this formal existence result; its earlier theorems remain.

C1.justification: The claimed local-SSL state of the art expands to include ImageNet. The introduction and Section 4 explicitly restrict BP parity to CIFAR-10, STL-10 and Tiny ImageNet, while the abstract adds ImageNet without similarly qualifying its parity sentence. The central theoretical and methodological contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses the remaining ImageNet gap and challenges of adapting local learning to residual connections. It adds the memory cost of fine spatial pooling and explains the activation-storage advantage of ideal local execution, while acknowledging that complete training with those ideal implementations was not performed.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository link and Algorithms 1–3 distinguishing ideal memory-saving execution from the implemented stop-gradient approach. It clarifies the existing pooled, concatenated linear readout and documents ImageNet architecture, adaptive pooling, optimizer schedule, hardware and training time. These substantially expand implementation and reproduction information.

R1.justification: V2 adds relevant references including SoftHebb, NoProp, scaling studies and VGG. Section 3.3 newly acknowledges related spatial pooling in Siddiqui et al.'s blockwise SSL, refining the mechanism's positioning. It also revises the Forward-forward objective description. The CPC reference's author/year update represents the same cited work, not a new one.

P1.justification: Section 3.3 receives a focused explanatory expansion, and the results and discussion receive targeted revisions. A new algorithm appendix precedes the retained appendix sequence. Grammar, affiliations, publication information and the erroneous template running header are updated, while most exposition and the overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains ImageNet and spatial-dependence columns and a SoftHebb row. V2 adds the resource table, ImageNet architecture table and three algorithm displays. Figure 5 and the appendix figures are relocated, with caption refinements; existing plotted content is retained rather than replaced by new analyses.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the spatial mechanism's theoretical justification and tests the central performance claim on ImageNet, revealing an important boundary to BP parity. The implementation documentation and qualified resource analysis also improve reproducibility and practical assessment. These gains outweigh the new predictive-coding numerical inconsistency and insufficiently qualified abstract wording. The resource savings remain estimates for ideal execution, rather than demonstrated savings over complete training runs.
